From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@elliosys.com>; Jonathan Mills <jonathan.mills@skybridge-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP private offer — hybrid seat + metered SKU and channel-margin waterfall

Hi Priya / Jonathan,

Thanks for taking the intro call yesterday. Quick follow-up: EllioSys is asking for a hybrid pricing model (flat seats for admin users + metered consumption for inference tokens) in the GCP private offer. Before we draft a term sheet, we need clarity on three things that will materially impact channel economics and the reseller split:

1) Expected commit cadence and how you expect consumption to ramp across Q1/Q2. (numbers by month help.)
2) Whether the reseller (Skybridge) must be compensated on list price or on net-of-discount revenue for metered usage.
3) Any co-term or true-up expectations at year end (they mentioned wanting a 10% buffer to avoid overages).

To make progress, can you send the monthly forecast you shared on the call (even a rough CSV) and confirm Skybridge's compensation trigger (list vs net)? Once we have that we can run a waterfall and propose a channel margin schedule that preserves your list-level incentives while keeping Redwood's committed revenue targets intact.

Cc'ing Ben/Irene/Tessa on channel math and execution. We'll produce a margin workback and a draft playbook for the PO.

Next steps: if you prefer, we can lock a 30-minute walk-through Friday afternoon to run the numbers live.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@elliosys.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — hybrid seat + metered SKU and channel-margin waterfall

Hi Naomi,

Thanks — quick answers below while I pull the spreadsheet:

- Forecast: Q1 month-by-month: Mar: $45k metered, Apr: $70k, May: $95k (metered spend). Seat licenses: 150 admins at $12/seat/mo (flat).
- Reseller comp: Skybridge expects to be paid on list price for seat ARR; for metered they prefer net-of-discount (they say market practice for usage).
- True-up: They want quarterly true-ups with a 10% cushion clause and the ability to request a one-time refund/credit if ramp is materially below plan.

Couple of clarifying questions for Redwood:
- Can you support two separate SKU lines in one private offer (seat SKU + metered SKU) with independent pass-through splits?
- Are there minimum list-price floors we must observe for marketplace listing if Skybridge is paid on list?

I'll attach the forecast CSV in a follow-up email. We can do Friday 3pm PT for a number run if that works.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Director, Cloud Procurement
EllioSys

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: GCP private offer — hybrid seat + metered SKU and channel-margin waterfall

Naomi / team,

Thanks — sketching some initial guardrails based on Priya's numbers. Attached is a simple margin_workback.xlsx with 3 scenarios (base, stretch, downside). High level:

- Seats: list $12/seat/mo; recommend 20% reseller pass-through (list-based) to preserve partner incentive.
- Metered: we should treat as net-of-discount for reseller comp (as Priya requested) but introduce a rebate corridor so Redwood keeps predictable ARR (suggest 5% net floor).
- True-up cadence: quarterly with single-year lookback; propose no cash refunds — give credits applied to future invoices (easier ops).

Risks / asks from ops:
- GCP private offers allow multiple SKUs, but accounting needs an explicit mapping for revenue recognition — ops will want to see the SKU id mapping before we finalize.
- If partner insists on list-based comp for metered usage, Redwood's unit economics fall below target in the downside ramp scenario (attached shows ~12% margin compression).

I'm happy to run the numbers live on Friday. Attaching margin_workback.xlsx for review.

Ben
Director, Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: GCP private offer — hybrid seat + metered SKU and channel-margin waterfall

Ben — good start. A couple of concrete edits / proposals:

- Use a two-tier waterfall for reseller comp on metered usage: first $0–$100k (gross month) = 15% on net; $100k+ = 10% on net. Keeps partner motivated early while protecting high-volume economics.
- Enforce a list-price floor for seat SKU in the marketplace listing (minimum $10/seat/mo) so partner comp calculations are predictable.
- For true-ups: quarterly reconciliation with credits only; include a clause that caps credits at 25% of that quarter's plan to prevent open-ended refunds.

Subject: Re: GCP private offer — hybrid seat + metered SKU and channel-margin waterfall

Priya / Jonathan — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the forecast.

Summary of what Redwood will propose in the draft PO:
- Two SKUs in the same private offer: Seat SKU (flat) + Metered SKU (usage).
- Seat comp: 20% of list (list floor $10/seat/mo).
- Metered comp: net-of-discount tiers: 0–100k gross/mo = 15% on net; >100k = 10% on net. Net calculation will exclude promotional credits and internal/dev projects.
- True-ups: quarterly reconciliation; credits only; credit cap 25% of quarter plan.
- Ops requirement: we need SKU id mapping and the monthly forecast CSV to lock revenue recognition and billing mapping.

Next steps:
- Priya, please send the CSV when you have it.
- I'm scheduling a 30-minute number run for Friday 15:00 PT (invites to follow).
- Ben / Irene / Tessa — I'll ask ops to draft the PO template and I'll attach the playbook.

Attaching the initial playbook snapshot for their review. If Skybridge insists on list-based comp for metered usage we will need to build a larger committed-minimum or tiered uplift to preserve unit economics; Ben, can you add a downside scenario to the sheet for that case?

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference
